THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 24.10.2016 PASSED IN MVC NO.72/2006 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE, &
MACT, NAGAMANGALA, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed under Section-173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellants-claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 24th October 2016, passed in MVC No.72/2006, on the file of the Senior Civil Judge & MACT,
Nagamangala, seeking enhancement of compensation.

2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the appellants and learned counsel for respondent No.2 - insurance company and perused the materials on record.
NC: 2024:KHC:21379 3.

The learned counsel for the appellants submit that the deceased was a civil contractor and the Tribunal has taken the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.4,000/-, which is on the lesser side contrary to the evidence on record and further quantum of compensation awarded under various Sri P P Harshith Gowda vs Ajith Madhukar Prabhu on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117062652/
2

sentences.text: heads is on the lesser side.
Therefore, seeks for enhancement of compensation.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for second respondent - insurance company submits that the Tribunal is justified in passing the impugned judgment and award and there is no ground for enhancement.
That the compensation amount as awarded by the Tribunal is sufficient and adequate.

5. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under various heads is as follows:
i) Loss of dependency : Rs.7,68,000-00 ii) Loss of estate : Rs. 20,000-00 iii) Loss of love and affection : Rs. 9,000-00 iv) Loss of consortium : Rs. 25,000-00 v) Funeral expenses : Rs. 25,000-00 NC: 2024:KHC:21379 vi) Loss of care and guidance for minor children : Rs. 25,000-00 ...............................
Total Rs. 8,72,000-00 6.
The occurrence of the accident, death of the deceased in the road traffic accident and coverage of insurance are not in dispute in this case.
7. The deceased was a civil contractor.
The Tribunal has taken monthly income of the deceased at Rs.4,000/- only, which is on the lesser side contrary to the evidence on record.
The claimants have produced the income tax details as per Ex.P6, Ex.P7, Ex.P18 and Ex.P20 and submits that the deceased was a civil contractor and earning Rs.8,00,000/- per annum.

Considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, the income of the deceased is assessed at Rs.7,000/-
per month.
The deceased was aged 33 years old.
Therefore, 40% of his monthly income is added towards future prospects.
The claimants are wife and two minor children.
Therefore, one-third of income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.
The appropriate multiplier is '16'.

Therefore, the compensation under the head of 'loss of dependency' is recalculated and quantified as follows:
NC: 2024:KHC:21379 {(Rs.7000 + Rs.2800) x 12 x 16 x 2/3rd } = Rs.12,54,400 8.

As per the principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017)
16 Supreme Court Cases 680, Rs.40,000/- to be awarded to each of the dependents Sri P P Harshith Gowda vs Ajith Madhukar Prabhu on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117062652/
3 towards loss of consortium.

sentences.text:
In the present case, the claimants, who are wife and two minor children are awarded Rs.40,000/- each i.e., Rs.1,20,000/-
(Rs.40,000 x 3) towards 'loss of consortium'.
Further, the compensation of Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards 'loss of estate' and Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards 'funeral expenses'.
As per the decision in the case of Pranay Sethi, the aforesaid amounts requires to be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

Therefore, I deem it appropriate to award Rs.1,32,000/-, Rs.16,500/- and Rs.16,500/-
respectively towards loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses respectively.
9. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.9,000/- towards 'loss of love and affection'.
'Loss of consortium' means 'loss of love and affection' and aggrieved cannot claim NC: 2024:KHC:21379 compensation for the same under two separate heads.

Since compensation of Rs.1,32,000/- is awarded towards loss of consortium, the claimants are not entitled for compensation of Rs.9,000/-
under the head of 'loss of love and affection'.
Ordered accordingly.
11. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.25,000/- towards 'loss of care and guidance for minor children'.
The same is just and proper and does not call for interference.
Accordingly, the same is kept intact.
12. Therefore, appellants/claimants are entitled for compensation under various heads as follows:

Sl.No. Head of compensation Amount of compensation awarded 1 Loss of dependency Rs. 12,54,400-00 2 Loss of consortium Rs. 1,32,000-00 3 Loss of estate Rs. 16,500-00 4 Funeral expenses Rs. 16,500-00 5 Loss of care and guidance Rs.
25,000-00 for minor children 6 Loss of love and affection Nil Total Rs.14,44,400-00 13.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:21379 ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The appellants/claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.14,44,400-00 as against Rs.8.72,000/- awarded by the Tribunal alongwith interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
iii) The impugned judgment and award dated 24th October 2016, passed in MVC No.72/2006, on the file of the Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Nagamangala is modified to the above extent.
iv) The enhanced compensation shall be deposited by the 2nd respondent/insurance company with interest at 6% per annum, within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of the judgment.
Sri P P Harshith Gowda vs Ajith Madhukar Prabhu on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117062652/
4 v) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the Tribunal shall stand intact.
vi) Draw award accordingly.
 NC: 2024:KHC:21379  vii) Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, alongwith certified copy of this judgment forthwith.
